hrcw: Work where there is a risk of a person falling more than 2 m
Demolition of an element of a structure that is load-bearing or related to physical integrity
Work likely to involve disturbing asbestos
Structural alterations or repairs that require temporary support
Work in or near a confined space
Work in or near a trench or shaft with an excavated depth greater than 1.5 m, or a tunnel
Work involving the use of explosives
Work on or near pressurised gas distribution mains or piping
Work on or near chemical, fuel or refrigerant lines
Work on or near energised electrical installations or services
Work in an area that may have a contaminated or flammable atmosphere
Work involving tilt-up or precast concrete elements
Work on, in or adjacent to a road, railway, shipping lane or other traffic corridor in use
Work in an area at a workplace in which there is any movement of powered mobile plant
Work in an area in which there are artificial extremes of temperature
Work in or near water or other liquid that involves a risk of drowning

workers.name: Sam Example
workers.roles: Licensed plumber; Drainer; Gasfitter; Supervisor / foreman

steps.step: Arrive, sign in, site induction, set up work area
hazards: Public / occupants entering the work area
Slips, trips and falls on uneven ground
controls: Barricade or tape off the work area; keep occupants and public out
Complete principal contractor / client site induction and sign in
Review this SWMS with all workers before starting. Workers sign the sign-on sheet
Check access routes; keep work area tidy and remove trip hazards

steps.step: Isolate electrical supply to equipment (e.g. electric hot water unit)
controls: Licensed person isolates supply at the switchboard; lock out and danger tag (personal lock per worker)
Test for dead before touching; re-test after any break
Locate cables in walls, floors and ceilings before cutting or drilling

steps.step: Isolate water (and gas / electricity, see the isolation steps) and drain the old unit
controls: Let the unit cool, or drain hot water to a safe outlet

steps.step: Remove the old unit and move in the new one
hazards: Possible asbestos in old cupboards, flues or sheeting
controls: Use an appliance trolley; two-person lift; plan the route and clear obstacles
Check for suspect asbestos before cutting or removing panels (see the asbestos steps if ticked)

steps.step: Install, connect and commission (tempering valve, relief valves, set temperature)
hazards: Scalding risk to occupants if delivery temperature is not limited
controls: Install a tempering or thermostatic mixing valve to the Plumbing Code; test the outlet temperature
Check all relief and drain lines discharge safely
Complete the compliance certificate and give the owner instructions

steps.step: Handle pipes, fittings, tools and materials
hazards: Strain or sprain from lifting, carrying or awkward postures
controls: Use trolleys, pipe racks and mechanical aids for heavy or long items
Team lift items over about 20 kg or awkward loads. Plan the route first
Rotate tasks for sustained kneeling or overhead work
Gloves; knee pads for kneeling work

steps.step: Use power and hand tools (cutting, drilling, threading)
controls: Use battery tools where practicable; guards fitted and working
Portable RCD on all plug-in equipment
Tools and leads tested and tagged (3-monthly on construction sites, AS/NZS 3012). Visual check before use
Safety glasses; hearing protection when noise is high (e.g. cutting, core drilling)

steps.step: Use hazardous chemicals (solvent cement and primer, sealants, drain cleaners, LPG)
controls: Use in ventilated areas; keep containers closed
Current SDS available on site. Follow SDS handling and first aid instructions
No ignition sources near flammable products
Chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection as per SDS

hazards: Unsecured openings or excavations left behind
controls: Remove waste; dispose of offcuts and chemical containers correctly
Leave no open excavation, pit or roof penetration unprotected
Report incidents and near misses to the supervisor the same day

ppe: Insulated gloves only where the electrical risk assessment requires them
references: Hazardous manual tasks Code of Practice
Managing the work environment and facilities Code of Practice
Managing electrical risks in the workplace Code of Practice
Work Health and Safety Act 2011 and Regulation (ACT: 2011; NSW: 2025). SWMS requirements: r 291 and r 299-303

emergency.call: Emergency: 000 (ask for ambulance, fire or police)
